missForest: Random Forest imputation

Source: R/Imputation.R
dot-imp_missForest.Rd

Which unit the forests learn from is set by observations:

  • "features" (default): the proteins are the observations and the samples the variables, so each sample is predicted from the other samples, with forests trained over thousands of proteins. This is the default of MsCoreUtils::impute_RF() and the orientation of knn and bpca here.

  • "samples": the samples are the observations and every protein is a variable, as NAguideR does. Each forest then trains on at most n - 1 samples, which suits large cohorts only.

Usage

.imp_missForest(x, args = list())

Arguments

args

list with optional observations ("features", the default, or "samples"), maxiter (default 10), ntree (default 100) and mtry (default floor(sqrt(p)) with "features", the missForest default, and floor(p^(1/3)) with "samples", NAguideR's cube root of the number of proteins). The fit is delegated to MsCoreUtils::impute_RF(), which gives identical results.

Details

Until NADIA 0.99.2 the only orientation was "samples". On nadia_dia (12 samples) with values hidden at random, the RMSE was 0.264 against 0.402, and on the TMT example 0.113 against 0.165 with 24 samples and 0.153 against 0.455 with 12 (Bioconductor review, #186).

This method is stochastic and takes no seed of its own, because missForest::missForest() does not accept one. To reproduce a run, call set.seed() before impute_proteomics(), as for every stochastic method in NADIA.
